praise: Your mall paragraph gave a reason for every single sense — soft clothes to touch, the food court to smell, the shops you want to visit to see. Five senses, five reasons, in order. That is a whole paragraph doing its job.

essay.summary: You opened by naming your place and what the paragraph was about, then took the senses one at a time with a "because" after each one, and you kept the order with Another, One more, Finally. Towards the end two sentences run into each other without a full stop, because you were going fast.

fixes.was: is hear I can hear all the people talking
fixes.should: is hear. I can hear all the people talking
fixes.why: Two sentences need a full stop between them. The same thing happens just after "is taste".
Senses take "of": the sense of sight, the sense of touch, the sense of smell.

fixes.was: 1 sense I can use at the mall
fixes.should: One sense I can use at the mall
fixes.why: Small numbers are written as words in a sentence — you did it yourself later with "One more sense".

essay.next: Read your last three sentences out loud and put a full stop wherever you stop for breath.

math.approach: On both of the subtract-and-simplify questions you kept the whole numbers and the fractions apart, and both subtractions were right: 5 3/4 − 1 1/4 came out as 4 2/4, and 2 5/6 − 1 1/6 as 1 4/6. Those are the correct amounts. Each one only needed the last step, cutting the fraction down: 2/4 is 1/2, and 4/6 is 2/3. On the page-numbers puzzle your 149 looks like 9 + 2 × 70, which is the right plan — count the one-digit pages, then two digits for each page after that — but pages 10 to 72 are 63 pages, not 70, so it comes to 9 + 126 = 135.
math.note: Two to look at again. In "Sara has 30 cards" you found 5, which is exactly what each friend gets — but the 4 she gives away comes out of Sara's own share, not theirs, so each friend keeps the 5. And ___ ÷ 4 = 20: if something is shared into 4 parts and each part is 20, the whole thing must be bigger than 20, so it is 4 × 20 = 80.
